name: Why do door frames in Denver and Aurora homes frequently shift and stick?

mainEntity.name: Why do door frames in Denver and Aurora homes frequently shift and stick?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homes across the Denver metro area, Aurora, and Centennial experience heavy seasonal shifts between dry winters and humid summer spells, along with expansive clay soils that can cause minor foundation settlement. These movements frequently pull standard door frames out of square, causing doors to bind, rub on top corners, or fail to latch. Proper installation requires anchoring jambs securely with quality shims and leaving adequate expansion gaps so framing movements do not jam the door slab as indoor humidity fluctuates throughout the year.
acceptedAnswer.description: Expansive soil movement and sharp seasonal humidity swings along the Front Range cause framing to shift, requiring careful shimming and proper clearance gaps during installation.
